title: Rapha to make WorldTour return with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe in 2027
content:
Cyclist
Rapha to make WorldTour return with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe in 2027

After a year spent away from pro cycling’s top division, British brand Rapha is set to make its return to the pro peloton with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe next year.

The team, home to Remco Evenepoel, Jai Hindley and Florian Lipowitz, will become the third WorldTour squad to wear Rapha’s threads in the pro peloton, following in the footsteps of Team Sky and EF Education-EasyPost. This time, the brand hopes Red Bull will be able to ‘win with character’, having focused heavily on cutting-edge R&D alongside Red Bull’s aero expert Dan Bigham.

The brand believes the partnership will ‘put Rapha back where it belongs, right back at the front of races’. Red Bull’s team boss Ralph Denk sees the collaboration with ‘huge potential for growth’, as he eyes up a ‘homecoming’ for Rapha on British roads at next summer’s Tour de France.

Cyclist spoke to some of the key names behind Rapha’s latest WorldTour foray.

Rapha’s WorldTour comeback

Rapha bowed out of the WorldTour at the end of 2025 when the brand parted ways with EF Education-EasyPost. The news came with the announcement of a new deal with the US national team, with the LA 2028 Olympics seen to be the big goal. At the time, then-CEO Fran Millar said that Rapha aimed to get back to the ‘forefront of the sport’. That time appears to have come after just one season out of the loop.

‘While we were out of the sport, we had plenty of time to do some soul-searching and work out what we wanted to do next,’ Joel Natale, Chief Product Officer at Rapha, says. ‘We were able to partner with a hugely dominant team in Team Sky and then with EF, who tried to bring something different to the sport with content, personality, disruption.

‘Ultimately, we could only go back into the sport if we could do both of those things at the same time. It would only be worth it if we win, but win with character.’

Rapha told Cyclist that it was in discussions with other WorldTour teams, including Visma-Lease a Bike. Clearly, Rapha was eager to get back onto the top division, but what is different about this partnership in comparison to its previous WorldTour dabbles?

‘EF was an incredible partner for Rapha, but it was massively different,’ Natale tells us. ‘The responsibility was on us, and the desire wasn’t really there. We did one big aero project with them for 2022 to try and get Stefan Bissegger in yellow. Otherwise, it was down to us. But they’re at the other end of the ranking, and they’re doing something completely different in racing.

‘We came to terms with the idea that the [EF] story on its own isn’t enough. You need to win and tell the story. Even if we could have run a UAE deal, the story has already been told.

‘Everyone knows what Red Bull has done in every sport,’ Natale continues. ‘This is a storied team, and they were winning long before Red Bull was here. So we want to put Rapha back where I think we belong, right back at the front of races, on the podium.’

‘Bora have pushed us on timelines, in terms of how tight they wanted to be able to make changes, the volume of kit that they wanted and having everything on another level. This R&D challenge is really exciting for us. We wouldn’t get the chance to work with such talent within every team. We are ready at Rapha to reset our image for a new generation of cyclists.’

Achieving ‘cycling’s potential’

Rapha is pairing up with Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, a squad that featured on the podiums of all three Grand Tours in 2026 and finished the season as the second-best team in the UCI rankings.

Its team boss Ralph Denk has been instrumental in the team’s growth over the past decade, including the Red Bull takeover in mid-2024. He believes having Rapha on board is a step toward transforming cycling’s audience.

‘When I was younger, cyclists looked like they were from the moon,’ Denk said at the launch of the partnership. ‘But now, cycling is a lifestyle, and for me, Rapha had a big part in making cycling bigger on a lifestyle level, not just a performance level.

‘The partnership is not just about performance, it’s about lifestyle. We were approached by several Italian brands. They make good cycling apparel, don’t get me wrong, but the combination of lifestyle and high performance, I see just one. Rapha.’

The London-based brand proved popular during its two previous WorldTour dabbles. With EF, Rapha attracted wide attention through switch-out kits in collaboration with streetwear brand Palace. During its time with Sky, then-CEO Simon Mottram told CityAM the brand ‘sold a lot of stuff’ on the back of the Team Sky deal. Denk is hoping for similar returns a decade on.

‘Cycling has huge potential in merchandising,’ Denk says. ‘In the Red Bull environment, we have all the numbers. What are the football teams, the Formula 1 teams’ revenue? For cycling, there is room to improve. I believe cycling has the same potential as Formula 1. Our mission is to make cycling bigger and we need different styles, both on bike and off bike.’

Team rider Callum Thornley has a more emotional connection to the new deal, stating that the partnership is a ‘big thing’ for a British rider like him.

‘I think my first pair of bib shorts were Rapha,’ the Scottish rider said. ‘It’s a full circle moment.’

‘It’s a scientific, knowledge-based arms race’

Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe’s Head of Engineering Dan Bigham has played a big role in the Rapha partnership. The aero boffin has been involved in the development of the kit since the spring, visiting wind-tunnels and creating a machine-learning system to chew the numbers. Two other aerodynamicists were taken on board as part of the Rapha-Red Bull deal – one a former McLaren’s F1 team employee, the other an expert in jellyfish movement.

‘There’s only so much knowledge published on cycling apparel out there right now,’ Bigham says. ‘The exciting bit is bringing that knowledge together with Rapha and being genuinely world-class at both so we understand the demands of the event and how we can influence that. We can execute that quicker than any other apparel manufacturer can.

‘We had full commitment when I told them [Rapha] everything we know and don’t know. That’s the frontier, and we want to push that forward. I was amazed by that because sometimes we pushed it a bit further than what’s sensible or reasonable.’

Bigham believes that riders could soon wear a different skinsuit each day, tailored to wind direction and racing ambitions. With Rapha, he’s building a database to support this.

‘[Aerodynamic] flow conditions change in every environment around the world, every rider where they’re riding in the bunch, whether you’re riding in a city, by a lake, whether it’s windy, raining. That changes the aerodynamic flow. It’s a complex optimisation problem, but with Rapha, we’re trying to find the true optimal flow solution for every rider.

‘We’re pulling it all together – mechanistic understanding of textiles through to measuring in the field. We’re building the full database we need, those causal links, so we can go to Rapha and say we need a sock for this exact condition, this exact race, this exact rider in the group. That’s the end goal, so we can do that quicker and more consistently than anyone else.

‘We’re closing in on this,’ Bigham says. ‘We’re probably only a few months away from at least having the bare-bones structure. It’s then a matter of feeding more data into that model and validating that model properly.

But does Bigham know Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe are a step ahead? He believes so.

‘There’s nothing in the literature, and there’s nothing that would explain why any other team or any other manufacturer has approached it with this methodology,’ he affirms. ‘From the things other teams say and what they do, it would imply that they probably are not [doing the same things as us].

‘It’s like throwing darts at a dartboard. Other teams would typically go to the wind-tunnel and do 20, 30, 40 fabrics and make two, three, four socks. They go to the wind-tunnel and test them on one or two riders. That’s quite logical, but we want to find the true nuance and have confidence to take it there. It’s multiple PhDs level of research. We don’t want to publish it. We want to contain that knowledge within Rapha Red Bull and beat everybody. It’s a scientific, knowledge-based arms race.

‘This R&D programme is not only unique, it’s absolutely game-changing. It’s quite scary how fast we’re moving.’

Details on the kit design are yet to be shared with the public, but we can expect the jersey to break cover once Red Bull host their team camp in Mallorca next month.
